newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela to have weekend knee surgery--spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to have weekend knee surgery--spokesman.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela will undergo a minor operation on his knee at a South African military hospital at the weekend, his spokesman announced on Friday.
"President Mandela will be going to the 1st Military Hospital in Pretoria for a very minor procedure on the right knee," presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters.
"He will be admitted early tomorrow morning (Saturday) and will be spending the night there. He will be discharged on Sunday morning," Mankahlana added.
He emphasised there was no need for concern over the president's health.
"He's fine. It's really insignificant. He'll be up and running on Sunday morning and carrying out his duties," the president's spokesman said.

Mandela's image as the man who led South Africa's relatively peaceful change from apartheid to democracy has led many foreign and domestic investors to regard him as essential to the country's stability.
To quell doubts about what will happen when he retires as head of state in 1999, Mandela, now 78, has endorsed Deputy President Thabo Mbeki as his successor.
